page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server belonging to the High Clock Speed instance family. Built on KVM virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core using an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps, includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and does not bundle local disk storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable general CPU throughput alongside specific memory bandwidth limitations. In synthetic tests, the instance records a stress-ng multi-core score of 8,310.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,720.0, placing both within the median distribution for its hardware tier. Software compilation through Clang registers 7,775.0 points in Geekbench, and Redis SET throughput achieves 8.09 million operations per second. Conversely, memory subsystem benchmarks reveal lower relative bandwidth; uncached large-block read operations register at 37.74 GB/sec and PassMark memory testing scored 1,525.1, both ranking in the lower 25th percentile. Similarly, PassMark database operations and physics tests reflect constrained scores, and medium-tier language model inference (7B model) yields only 5.16 tokens per second during generation.

From an engineering and resource allocation perspective, the lack of onboard storage and modest uncached memory throughput make this instance less suited for I/O-intensive databases or heavy in-memory data processing. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and AVX-512 extensions provide predictable per-thread instruction capability. It functions as a cost-efficient platform for CPU-bound batch compute pipelines, software build automation, CI/CD runners, and horizontal web application serving where network-attached block storage and balanced compute cycles are sufficient.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the High Clock Speed family, powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor. Operating under a KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, accompanied by 16 GiB of memory. This produces a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation typical of compute-optimized nodes. The CPU integrates 33 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16. The instance provides 3 Gbps of baseline networking capacity and includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes. Benchmark evaluations position the instance squarely in the middle tier for CPU-bound tasks, recording 4,720 in Geekbench multi-core and 8.09 million Redis SET operations per second. However, memory-intensive routines and database benchmarks score in the lower quartile due to constrained uncached memory bandwidth. It serves as an efficient choice for CI/CD compilation, batch compute, and standard web serving.
